compile.schedule: interfaces ≫ readMiss ≫ write ≫ evict ≫ countWb ≫ clear

explain: countWb's guard reads valid and dirty. After evict in the same cycle, both are already cleared, so the guard is never true and writebacks stays 0. Run before evict, it sees the dirty line and counts it. You can also add writebacks <= dirty[req_line] ? writebacks + 1 : writebacks; to evict and drop countWb.
diff: -- the three op rules all write `valid`: they must be chained, not ∥
-  schedule readMiss ≫ write ≫ evict ≫ countWb ≫ clear;
+  schedule readMiss ≫ write ≫ countWb ≫ evict ≫ clear;

explain: flush writes dirty, which write and evict also write, so it joins the ≫ chain. Only one op is valid per cycle, so its position in the chain does not matter. The stimulus writes lines 1 and 2 (io_dirty = 6) and flushes at cycle 3, after which io_dirty reads 0.
